title: Internal Hom on $\Dctf$ at all coefficient stages
statement:
Use the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, with $p\ne\ell$, and let $X$ be separated of finite type over $k$. An admissible coefficient $\Lambda$ is one of the pulled-back condensed rings $A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of [sk-def-localizing-closure], with $A$ finite commutative and killed by a power of $\ell$, and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite. Use $\Dctf$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], the ambient relative derived tensor and internal Hom of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], and $a^!$ of [sk-prop-sf-existence]. A locally constant perfect complex on a scheme $S$ means a complex which, on a pro-étale cover, is the scalar extension to $\Lambda_S$ of a bounded complex of finite projective $\Lambda(*)$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex, def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. The extension $a_!$ for a locally closed immersion $a=i\circ u$ is $i_*u_!$, with $u$ open and $i$ closed, acting termwise [det-lem-int-tensor-projection].

Let $\Lambda$ be admissible. For $K,L\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$,
$\cHom_\Lambda(K,L)\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$. More precisely, if
$a:S\hookrightarrow X$ is a locally closed immersion and $P$ a locally constant
perfect complex on $S$, then

$$
\cHom_X(a_!P,L)\simeq Ra_*\cHom_S(P,a^!L)\simeq Ra_*(P^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}a^!L),
\qquad P^\vee=\cHom_S(P,\Lambda_S),
$$

in $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, and every $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ is obtained
from finitely many objects $a_!P$ of this form by shifts and cones.

proof.text: The scheme and coefficient conventions are [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] and [sk-def-localizing-closure]. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes all standing schemes Noetherian, hence qcqs; their open subsets are quasi-compact. The coefficient pullbacks are exact and identify the inverse-image coefficient rings by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. We will use only the relative module-sheaf operations over these rings, including the completed integral coefficient sheaf, never tensor over the discrete scalar field in place of the condensed field.

source.place: Paragraph 1, standing conventions and finite stratifications.

proof.text: The categories $\Dctf$ are triangulated. For finite $A$, constructible sheaves are weak Serre by [lem-sfb-discrete-noetherian-constructible-serre], so [prop-weil-pbc-module-bounded-constructible-triangulated], with coefficient category $\Ab$ and ring object $A_X$, makes $\Dbc$ triangulated. For integral coefficients use [sk-lem-int-integral-heart](1), and for rational coefficients use [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-triangulated]. Finally [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude] makes finite Tor amplitude thick and identifies $\Dctf$ with its intersection with $\Dbc$. These facts give closure under zero, isomorphisms, finite cones and shifts in every coefficient case.

source.place: Paragraphs 1 and 3, the triangulated closure used in dévissage.

proof.text: We spell out the finite stratification dévissage used below. By the geometric clause (1) of [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification], any given finite locally closed stratification can be refined and ordered $S_1,\ldots,S_m$ with $V_r=S_1\cup\cdots\cup S_r$ open. This clause is independent of its auxiliary coefficient $E$ or $\Qlb$; fix $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ when applying it even to finite or integral coefficient objects. For a complex $C$ adapted to these strata, let $v_r:V_r\hookrightarrow X$ and put $C_r=v_{r!}v_r^*C$ on $X$. Apply the short exact open--closed sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] termwise on $V_r$ to its open $V_{r-1}$ and closed complement $S_r$. Exact extension by zero gives a degreewise short exact sequence $0\to C_{r-1}\to C_r\to a_{r!}(C|_{S_r})\to0$. The corresponding derived triangle is [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. The composition and factorization identifications, including agreement of closed-then-open with open-then-closed extension, are precisely [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence]. With $C_0=0$ and $C_m=C$, induction on $r$ expresses $C$ as finite cones of the displayed pieces. Exactness also shows that the same construction applies to any representing complex, independently of its representative.

source.place: Paragraph 1, open--closed localization triangles, expanded as a finite filtration.

proof.text: For finite $A$, use [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] to descend $K$ to an étale bounded constructible finite-Tor complex, and choose an ordered Tor interval $[a,b]$. The finite ring $A$ is Noetherian, since each ideal is a finite set of generators. By [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible] choose a bounded complex $F$ of flat constructible sheaves representing the descent. On a common finite stratification of the étale terms [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-stratification-intersection], each term has a finite locally constant $A$-module model. Check its flatness on the étale site, before pulling back: for a geometric point $x$ of the stratum and any scalar $A$-module $M$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the geometric-point inverse image and $F^r\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\underline M$. Exactness of the étale stalk functor [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and flatness of $F^r$ imply that $F^r_x\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M$ is concentrated in degree zero. Thus the scalar model $F^r_x$ is flat. It is finitely presented: it is finite, and the kernel of a finite free surjection onto it is finitely generated by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. Now [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-flat-module-projective] makes this model finite projective. Pull $F$ back exactly to the pro-étale site. Its étale local constant models give pro-étale local constant models on the same strata. Apply Step 3 to each of the finitely many terms. Each term is consequently obtained by finite cones of sheaves $a_!P$ with $P$ locally constant finite projective in degree zero. The stupid truncations of the bounded complex $F$ have degreewise split short exact successive sequences with quotients $F^r[-r]$; [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] supplies their triangles. Induction through its finitely many nonzero degrees proves the required finite-cone-and-shift generation of $K$. In particular this does not replace a finite-Tor complex by its cohomology sheaves.

source.place: Paragraph 1, finite coefficients: bounded flat model and its stupid filtration.

proof.text: For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, clause (1) of [det-lem-int-integral-heart-local-model] gives a finite stratification on which $K$ is pro-étale locally the completed scalar extension of a bounded complex of finite free $\mathcal O_E$-modules. Thus each restriction is a locally constant perfect complex in the statement's sense. Apply Step 3 directly to $K$ on this stratification, giving finitely many pieces $a_!(K|_S)$ and no retract operation. The case $\mathbf Z_\ell$ is $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, [det-lem-coefficient-heart-filtration] gives a finite filtration of each constructible cohomology sheaf by $a_!P$ with $P$ lisse finite free, hence perfect in degree zero. Since $K$ is bounded, finitely many truncation triangles [lem-pc-derived-lower-truncation-step-triangle], followed by the triangles of these sheaf filtrations [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle], express $K$ by finite cones and shifts of those pieces. This includes $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and proves the generation clause at every stage.

source.place: Paragraph 1, integral and rational local models; the separate finite generation arguments.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality], $P^\vee$ is perfect and $\cHom_S(P,N)\simeq P^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}N$ for every ambient $N$. The slice-restriction assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] identifies its restrictions with the duals of the local models. The scalar-cohomology formulas of [lem-sfb-internal-hom-dual-constructible-models] apply to the locally constant perfect models in the statement and put both $P$ and $P^\vee$ in $\Dbc(S,\Lambda)$, including completed integral coefficients. Finite Tor amplitude is established separately in Step 7.

source.place: Paragraph 2, perfect dual and tensor-Hom formula; paragraph 3, membership of the perfect factors.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-internal-hom-dual-tor-amplitude] to the same local scalar models. It gives a single interval $[a,b]$ for $P$ and $[-b,-a]$ for $P^\vee$, tested against every module sheaf; for empty $S$ it gives $[0,0]$. Together with the bounded-constructibility conclusion of Step 6 and the definition [sk-def-sfb-constructible], this proves $P,P^\vee\in\Dctf(S,\Lambda)$. This uses no finite global dimension assumption on a finite coefficient ring.

source.place: Paragraph 2, perfect dual and tensor-Hom formula; paragraph 3, membership of the perfect factors.

proof.text: Let $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ be as in the statement. By [lem-pqf-qc-immersion-open-closed-factor], write it $S\xrightarrow{u}Z\xrightarrow{i}X$ with $u$ open and $i$ closed, and let $j:X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$ be the complementary open. Put $T=u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZL$, using the ambient derived support adjoint of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-adjunction]. Its fiber formula is $R\underline\Gamma_ZL\simeq i^*\operatorname{fib}(L\to Rj_*j^*L)$. Each of $j^*$, $Rj_*$ and $i^*$ preserves $\Dctf$ by [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images](1),(3). Step 2 therefore puts this fiber and then $R\underline\Gamma_ZL$ in $\Dctf$, and the same node's pullback clause puts $T$ in $\Dctf(S,\Lambda)$. This establishes support preservation without inferring it from existence of a right adjoint.

source.place: Paragraphs 2 and 3, locally closed support and preservation, with the ambient support object made explicit.

proof.text: The closed immersion $i$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a), so $(u,i)$ is a compactification of $a$. It computes $Ra_!=Ri_*u_!=i_*u_!=a_!$, because $i_*$ and $u_!$ are exact [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]; this is the compactification formula of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek]. Its comparison with the chosen compactification on the localizing closure is [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle]. For any $B\in\Loc(\Dctf(S,\Lambda))$, the ambient adjunction $i_*\dashv R\underline\Gamma_Z$ [det-lem-formal-closed-support-adjunction], followed by the ambient derived open adjunction $u_!\dashv u^*$ [def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek-adjunction], gives $\Hom_X(a_!B,L)\cong\Hom_S(B,T)$. By [sk-prop-sf-existence], the same functor is represented by $a^!L$. Both representing objects lie in the full localizing closure: $T$ by Step 8, and $a^!L$ by its definition. Transpose each counit under the other adjunction; the two resulting maps $T\rightleftarrows a^!L$ compose to the identities by the adjunction triangle identities. Thus $T\simeq a^!L$, naturally in $L$. This comparison tests only objects of the localizing closure, where that adjunction is actually defined.

source.place: Paragraph 2, trivial compactification and adjunction, repairing the scope of the Yoneda argument.

proof.text:
Now apply the ambient internal-Hom formulas of [lem-sfb-open-closed-internal-hom-formulas], first to $i$ and then to $u$ with target $R\underline\Gamma_ZL$. They give
$$\cHom_X(i_*u_!P,L)\simeq i_*\cHom_Z(u_!P,R\underline\Gamma_ZL)\simeq i_*Ru_*\cHom_S(P,u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZL).$$
The ringed-topos composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], with exact $i_*$, identifies $i_*Ru_*=Ra_*$. Step 9 replaces $u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZL$ by $a^!L$. We obtain the first stated isomorphism in the entire ambient $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, naturally in $P,L$. Unlike a calculation of global Hom alone, the cited formulas are identities of internal sheaf-valued derived Hom, without constructibility assumptions.

source.place: Paragraph 2, first internal-Hom isomorphism, using ambient open/closed internal adjunction.

proof.text: Step 6 with $N=a^!L$ gives the second isomorphism after applying $Ra_*$. Steps 8 and 9 give $a^!L\in\Dctf$, and Steps 6 and 7 give $P^\vee\in\Dctf$. The tensor and direct-image clauses of [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images](1),(3) therefore show that $Ra_*(P^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}a^!L)$ belongs to $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$. By Step 10 this is $\cHom_X(a_!P,L)$, proving membership for every generator and both displayed isomorphisms.

source.place: Paragraphs 2 and 3, second isomorphism and membership of each generator.

proof.text: Fix $L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], $\cHom(-,L)$ sends distinguished triangles contravariantly to distinguished triangles and commutes with shifts with the opposite sign. Step 2 therefore shows that the objects $B$ for which $\cHom(B,L)\in\Dctf$ form a full triangulated class: a triangle with two vertices satisfying the property has the third by the image triangle. It contains all $a_!P$ by Step 11. The finite constructions of Steps 3--5 now prove the property for every $K\in\Dctf$. Only finitely many cones and shifts have been used, exactly as asserted.

source.place: Paragraphs 1 and 3, exactness of internal Hom and the final finite dévissage.

proof_origin.place: All three paragraphs, with the support-adjunction scope repaired using ambient open/closed formulas, and coefficient-specific generation expanded.
